scope: Theorem 14.1 of the manuscript “Prefix Instructions and Incompressible Flows” (preprints/Prefix-Instructions-and-Incompressible-Flows-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8cd581420ec9967a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 48. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: At fixed positive computable viscosity, a deterministic one-tape machine and finite input effectively determine a smooth mean-zero general force on the unit torus such that, for every k ≥ 0 and spatial multi-index β, ∥∂k t ∂β x f(t)∥∞ ≤ Ck,β(1 + t)−1 . (18) Its zero-data Navier–Stokes solution is globally smooth and unique in the classical periodic comparison class, with uniformly bounded kinetic energy and mean-zero pressure. For the fixed label and open set y∗ = (1/2, 1/2, 1/4), O = {(x1, x2, z) : 1/2 < x1 < 1, 0 < z < 1/8}, (19) its material trajectory enters O exactly when the machine halts. Samples encode the full machine computation through the first halt, or indefinitely if there is none. The prescription uses only the finite table and input; arbitrary fixed real positive viscosity is allowed as a relative coefficient.
